We expect you to have:

  • 6+ years of experience in Accounts Payable or Finance Operations, including experience with complex or business-critical entities
  • Demonstrated ability to handle non-standard situations independently and apply senior judgment
  • Experience as a point of contact for business stakeholders - comfortable managing expectations and resolving operational issues directly
  • Strong experience with month-end close, reconciliations and AP controls
  • Solid working knowledge of NetSuite and Blackline; familiarity with Zip is a strong advantage
  • Experience in multi-currency, multi-entity or multi-country AP environments
  • Track record of informally developing or mentoring more junior colleagues
  • Excellent written and verbal English - English is our primary working language and the expected standard of communication throughout the team

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience supporting external audits and working with auditors directly
  • Exposure to process improvement projects or a continuous improvement methodology
  • Additional European language skills

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

title: Anaesthetic (Pain) Consultant
description:
At Montu UK, we are passionate about improving the lives of patients who have often exhausted conventional treatment options. Through our Alternaleaf clinic, we are helping people living with chronic and debilitating conditions access treatments that can make a genuine difference to their quality of life.

We are looking for Consultant Anaesthetists who are interested in exploring the growing field of medical cannabis and developing their expertise in chronic pain management.

This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a rapidly growing healthcare organisation, working alongside a multidisciplinary team of experienced clinicians who share a passion for improving patient outcomes.

With a fully funded Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management and comprehensive specialist training, we are keen to hear from consultants who are open to exploring new approaches to patient care and want to make a meaningful difference in an evolving area of medicine.

Previous chronic pain experience is not essential. What matters is a genuine interest in learning, an open-minded approach to alternative treatment options and a commitment to delivering excellent patient care.

What is the job?

As a Consultant Anaesthetist at Montu, the role focuses on assessing and supporting patients living with chronic pain who may have exhausted conventional treatment options.

Working within our Alternaleaf clinic, consultants play a central role in determining the suitability of cannabis-based prescription medicines (CBPMs), developing individualised treatment plans and supporting patients throughout their treatment journey.

The position offers the opportunity to build on existing expertise in analgesic pharmacology, pain management and opioid stewardship while developing specialist knowledge in an evolving area of medicine.

Our multidisciplinary approach brings together consultants, nurses, pharmacists and other healthcare professionals, allowing consultants to focus on clinical assessment, prescribing decisions and ongoing patient care.

Sponsored Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management

As part of our commitment to clinical development, Montu is offering a fully funded Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management through the University of South Wales, delivered fully online in partnership with Learna.

The programme provides an opportunity to develop specialist knowledge in chronic pain management while continuing to gain practical clinical experience within our multidisciplinary team.

About the diploma

  • A 12-month, part-time postgraduate diploma with all teaching and assessment completed online.

  • Focuses on interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary pain management, assessment and service provision.

  • Full course fees funded by Montu UK.

  • Two hours of protected, paid study time each week.

Further information about the programme is available through the University of South Wales.

Eligibility

  • A minimum working commitment of 24 hours per week with Montu.

  • Two of those hours each week are allocated as protected, paid study time.

  • Continued employment with Montu at a minimum of 24 hours per week for the duration of the diploma.

What will you be doing?

  • Providing high-quality care for patients seeking medical cannabis treatment for chronic pain and other qualifying conditions.

  • Conducting patient consultations, including clinical assessments, prescribing decisions and ongoing patient management.

  • Applying anaesthetic expertise in analgesic pharmacology, drug interactions and opioid stewardship to support safe prescribing.

  • Reviewing patient progress and treatment effectiveness, making adjustments where clinically appropriate.

  • Engaging in clinical outcome data collection to support evidence-based practice.

  • Contributing to clinical governance and maintaining robust patient care standards.

  • Collaborating with a multidisciplinary team, including nurses and pharmacists.

  • Completing the sponsored Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management alongside clinical responsibilities.

  • Participating in ongoing training and professional development, including specialist training in cannabis-based prescription medicines.

What you need

  • Full GMC registration with a current licence to practise.

  • Completion of specialist training in Anaesthesia (CCT/CCST) or equivalent.

  • Entry on the GMC Specialist Register for Anaesthesia.

  • Strong knowledge of analgesic pharmacology, pain management and safe prescribing.

  • Excellent communication skills and a patient-centred approach to care.

  • Ability to work independently while contributing to a multidisciplinary clinical team.

  • A strong interest in chronic pain and alternative treatment options.

  • Willingness to participate in clinical outcome data collection and reporting.

  • Ability to commit to a minimum of 24 hours per week for the duration of the diploma.

Previous chronic pain experience is welcome but not essential, as the sponsored diploma and comprehensive in-house training will support professional development.

Why join us?

  • Competitive Salary: £170,000 FTE, pro rata for contracted hours.

  • Funded Postgraduate Diploma: Full course fees for the Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management, plus two hours of protected, paid study time each week.

  • Flexible Working: Fully remote working with flexible clinical sessions and a minimum commitment of 24 hours per week.

  • Comprehensive Indemnity Coverage: Montu covers all professional and clinical indemnity insurance for work undertaken within the role.

  • Work-Life Balance: No night shifts or on-call requirements.

  • Specialist Training: Access to CPD-accredited medical cannabis education and specialist training from experienced clinicians.

  • Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals.

  • Professional Development: Build expertise in chronic pain management and contribute to an evolving area of medicine.

Training & Development

  • Fully funded Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management through the University of South Wales.

  • Regular CPD sessions to support ongoing professional development, appraisal and revalidation.

  • Specialist training delivered by experts, including Prof Anup Mathew (Consultant Psychiatrist) and Dr Gerard Sinovich (Pain Management Consultant).

  • Ongoing support and training in clinical protocols, prescribing practices and Montu's clinical systems.

  • Appraisal and revalidation support where Montu is the main employer.

Working arrangements

  • Remote Role: Fully remote working with flexibility around working days and hours.

  • Weekly Commitment: A minimum of 24 hours per week, consisting of 22 hours of clinical work and two hours of protected, paid study time.

  • Sessions: Standard clinical sessions consist of four hours of patient consultations, with flexibility to arrange sessions around preferred working days and hours.

  • Appointment Durations: 15 minutes for new and existing patients.

  • Multidisciplinary Support: Nurses and pharmacists support pre-consultation and follow-up prescribing tasks, allowing consultants to focus on clinical assessment, prescribing and patient care.

Our multidisciplinary model enables consultants to focus on their clinical expertise while benefiting from the support of an experienced wider healthcare team.

What we offer

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year two) + 8 bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

  • Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, and more

  • Growth Opportunities: Collaborate across teams and represent Montu at events, with support to grow your skills and impact

  • Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave

Postgraduate Diploma Sponsorship Terms and Conditions

As Montu is fully funding the Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management, sponsorship is subject to a separate training agreement.

  • A minimum commitment of 24 hours per week is required throughout the diploma programme.

  • Two hours each week are allocated as protected, paid study time.

  • Continued employment with Montu at a minimum of 24 hours per week is required for the duration of the diploma.

  • If employment ends before completing the diploma or within 12 months of completion, repayment of the course fees will be required.

Full repayment terms will be outlined in a separate training agreement, which must be reviewed and signed before enrolment.

About Us

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patient access to safe and effective treatments. Our mission is to transform lives by combining innovative technology with high-quality clinical care, ensuring patients receive the support they need at every step of their journey.

As a fast-growing organisation, we offer a collaborative and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers while contributing to meaningful change in healthcare. At Montu UK, your work has a direct impact on improving patients’ lives and expanding access to modern medical treatments.

title: Mid-Market Account Executive
description:
I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy.

I started Anima to change that.

Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima.

We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions.

Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them.

If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives.

-- Shun

Do you want to save lives with every clinic that you onboard?

Please note that as this role may involve site work and on-site support for our users, we can only consider your application if you are based in the UK. You will not be able to complete our screening task if you are not based in the UK, so please bear this in mind when submitting your application. We hope to welcome you to the team soon!

Join Anima, and you'll use your influence and people skills to get Anima into clinics and entire regions: an urgently needed product that saves lives amid critical levels of patient demand, with healthcare systems in crisis across the globe.

Since launching in the UK, we're now used in by GP practices, primary care networks and federations across the country who collectively provide care for over 2 million patients.

Have amazing stakeholder conversations with users who fanatically love the product, and steer our product direction

Our current distribution team have said that one of the biggest perks of working at Anima is seeing the delight and disbelief on people’s faces when we show them our demo, something that is truly a 10x generational leap. Here’s what some of our users have been saying:

*“I sent a plan to the patient and it’s incredible, within a few minutes they’re coming back to me saying that they can make the appointment!”

"I would call that next generation, I think you have that badge"

”Sometimes you need to stop driving a Fiesta and buy a Mercedes"*

Lots of us went into medicine because we wanted to maximise our positive impact. At Anima, we understand that distribution is the other half of a legendary product. Here are incredible things we’ve built as a result of our fullstack sales team:

  • A Clinical Director at one of our practices wanted to streamline multiple access channels and make access equitable and fair. After some great discovery and deep listening, the AM together with the customer suggested we build something called ‘proxy requests’, which would allow the reception team at a clinic to complete Anima requests on behalf of a patient who was on a landline call - this made it possible to give someone with no internet or mobile phone the same access to care. This is now one of our most popular features that has led to viral referrals and fanatical users.

  • One of our fullstack account manager, realised that adding a configurable feature that allows patients to self-book appointments directly into the electronic health record calendar would be critical to closing large enterprise accounts. By deeply understanding the pain points and anxieties underlying the feature, Anima built the feature in 9 days, to the great excitement of users at demo calls and $1m+ ACV meetings.

  • Off the back of fanatical referrals from our existing users, the team was invited to present to NHS England at national and regional level, and we’ve been helping to shape the future of the primary care market through an upcoming $1bn+ procurement framework.

Does this sound like you?

  • Hungry and wants their shot to change the world - a force of nature when empowered with the tools, resources and development to do it.

  • Exceptional communicator, able to distill complex information into clear and concise bullets without jargon. An excellent conduit between users and the rest of the company.

  • Able to execute a high sigma discovery process and in combination with incisive people intuition, elucidate deep pain points and opportunities to excite within minutes of the first call.

  • Has incredibly high standards for themselves and an unshakeable growth mindset: able to challenge themselves and those around them to push to do things better.

  • Exceptionally organised: able to build & maintain multiple relationships across a diverse range of organisations, and consistently execute on plans to onboard and retain users. Reliably follows up on 100% of qualified leads at optimal intervals.

  • A gifted relationship builder, able to quickly build rapport and emotional anchors with almost anyone and any persona.

  • Pragmatic rather than dogmatic in decision making: able to weigh real world data appropriately, changing course when necessary towards optimal outcomes for patients and clinicians.

  • Keen to understand the big picture & entire context of the company and vertical; impatient to grow towards a senior executive role.

  • Seeks to maximise combined team productivity, communicating the right things at the right time through the right channels.

  • Intellectually curious and loves learning - able to tackle entirely novel challenges that lack prior precedent through first principles thinking, creatively using the right pragmatic approach, with an understanding of alternatives and trade offs.

It's helpful to have B2B/SaaS experience, generating leads of $10k+ ACV, but not mandatory - we will make exceptions if you’re a high performing BDR. You need to have demonstrated a high growth mindset and potential for rapid skill development through past projects. For this role, you will need to be based in the UK.

Our current users & what to expect from the role

We're live with GP teams across the country, being used by teams across the NHS. Over the rest of 2024, we're continuing to onboard teams that want to build the future of healthcare, and will be working with the NHS to deploy Anima at regional & national level. We’ll also be identifying international partners to power Anima’s next stage of growth.

We’re looking to add talented account executives who understand the urgency and importance of what we’re doing for society and are hungry to make impact.

Our VP Sales has a 90%+ e2e close rate, and the distro org averages about 80%. Our CAC payback, gross margin, retention are all world class and you'll be joining an exceptional team with top metrics for SaaS, despite being in a traditionally slower vertical.

First month - some examples of what to expect:

  • Participate in user discovery & demo calls to develop a deep understanding of their fundamental motivations and needs/pain points, translating these insights into optimal feature roadmaps.

  • Source leads and execute campaigns. Get as much exposure as possible to developing the full lifecycle of an opportunity from lead through to closure.

  • Join the team at events & conferences, speaking to potential users, conducting demos and converting leads.

Next 6 months - some examples of what to expect:

  • Build domain expertise to scale our prospecting, identifying the teams in the most pain who are likely to become fanatical users of Anima.

  • Become the central point of contact for assigned GP practices and PCNs. Your job is to maximise discounted fanaticism, doing whatever is necessary to help practices start - and continue - using Anima.

  • Work with customer success colleagues to maximise virality and fanaticism across your accounts, doing whatever is needed to ensure every account leads to the maximum number of fanatical referrals.

6+ months - some examples of what to expect:

  • Potential to transition into a Strategic Enterprise AE, with managerial responsibility for junior AEs joining the team.

  • Take on account management responsibility for larger accounts e.g. GP federations and ICSs (covering 1m+ patients).

  • Work with the team to scale our sales & marketing, including working with NHS leaders to identify and secure regional & national-level procurement opportunities, including those beyond primary care.

What we offer

Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with:

  • Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off.

  • Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance.

  • Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay.

  • Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you.

  • Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development.

  • Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month.

  • Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget.

  • Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico.

  • Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week.

Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

title: Machine Learning Engineering Manager II
description:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we’re behind some of Spotify’s most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

At Spotify, great personalization is about more than recommending the right song. It's about creating listening experiences that feel effortless and meaningful while balancing the needs of listeners, creators, and our business.
The Samba team, part of Spotify's Personalization Mission, works on multi-objective balancing and sequencing for personalized listening experiences like Autoplay, Radio, and Mixes. Our engineers bring together machine learning, backend engineering, and data engineering to build systems that support Spotify's financial objectives while keeping listeners at the center of what we do.

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead this team, develop our engineers, and help shape the technical direction of systems that influence how millions of people experience Spotify.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and grow a team of machine learning, backend, and data engineers, supporting their development and helping them deliver their best work.Shape the team's technical strategy and execution, ensuring engineering efforts align with listener needs and Spotify's broader business goals.
  • Guide the development of machine learning and recommendation systems that balance multiple objectives across personalized listening experiences.
  • Collaborate with Product and engineering partners to define priorities, align on outcomes, and translate complex challenges into clear plans.
  • Support the team in making thoughtful technical decisions across experimentation, scalability, system reliability, and model performance.
  • Create a culture of ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement, where engineers feel empowered to experiment and learn.
  • Drive effective planning and delivery while balancing immediate priorities with long-term technical health.
  • Foster an inclusive, supportive team environment through coaching, feedback, and thoughtful people leadership.

Who You Are

  • You have experience managing and developing engineering teams, with a track record of helping people grow and delivering impactful results.
  • You bring a strong technical background in machine learning, software engineering, or related areas, and can confidently guide technical conversations.
  • You understand the opportunities and challenges of developing and operating machine learning systems in production.
  • You have experience working with cross-functional partners to define priorities, navigate trade-offs, and deliver against shared goals.
  • You are comfortable leading teams through ambiguity and helping engineers make informed technical decisions.
  • You care about building inclusive, collaborative environments where people feel supported and empowered.
  • You communicate with clarity, lead with empathy, and know how to balance people, technology, and business needs

Where You'll Be

  • This role is based in Stockholm or London
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Compensation

Additional Information

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.

At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

title: Engineering Manager, Ads Product Catalogs
description:
Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com.

This role is open to candidates based in the UK or the Netherlands.

Reddit is where people come to discover, research, and discuss products that inform their purchasing decisions. Shopping, across advertising and organic experiences, is a high priority for the company, and product catalogs are foundational to that work.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead Reddit’s Product Catalogs team. You will lead a full-stack engineering team responsible for the infrastructure and advertiser-facing experiences that help thousands of advertisers onboard, organize, and manage millions of products. Your team will build intuitive UIs, robust APIs, and scalable backend systems for catalog ingestion, storage, and product data management.

These systems power Dynamic Product Ads (DPA) and organic shopping, connecting users with relevant products in the context of their interests and conversations. Someone browsing r/golf might discover popular golf clubs, while someone reading a discussion about sunglasses in r/BuyItForLife might see the exact models being discussed. Your team will make it easier for advertisers to bring their products to Reddit and participate in these moments of discovery.

In this role, you will set technical direction, develop engineers, and drive execution across the catalog platform and advertiser experience. You will work closely with cross-functional partners to understand customer needs and make catalog onboarding and management seamless. You will also partner with Reddit’s Knowledge Graph teams to support organic shopping experiences.

This role calls for strong technical judgment, people leadership, and a focus on customer needs. It is based in Reddit’s Amsterdam or London office, with a team working across European time zones.

Responsibilities:

  • Create a world class catalogs system that can scale to support billions of products
  • Work closely with product managers and designers to craft compelling user experiences
  • Collaborate with a wide range of teams from Ad Formats to Ad Delivery to ensure successful end-to-end delivery of product ads
  • Establish and manage to SLAs within your team
  • Be a strong mentor and cross-functional advocate for your team
  • Contribute meaningfully to team strategy. We give everyone a seat at the table and encourage active participation in planning for the future. Don’t just come along for the ride.

Required Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience in backend or full stack product development
  • 2+ years of experience managing engineering teams
  • You're highly technical, enough to solve almost any problem your team has yourself, but you prefer to guide your team into solving them.
  • Ability to work independently. You’ll be working with stakeholders that are mostly based in North America. You need to be able to make decisions and solve problems autonomously.
  • Excellent communication skills. You must be able to collaborate effectively with teams in a fully-remote environment and discuss complex topics with technical and non-technical audiences.

Benefits:

  • Global Benefit programs that fit your lifestyle, from workspace to professional development to caregiving support
  • Family Planning Support
  • Gender-Affirming Care
  • Mental Health & Coaching Benefits
  • Group Personal Pension Scheme with Employer match
  • Private Medical and Dental Scheme
  • Income Replacement Programs
  • Bike to Work scheme
  • Flexible Vacation & Paid Volunteer Time Off
  • Generous Paid Parental Leave

In select roles and locations, the interviews will be recorded, transcribed and summarized by artificial intelligence (AI). You will have the opportunity to opt out of recording, transcription and summarization prior to any scheduled interviews.

During the interview, we will collect the following categories of personal information: Identifiers, Professional and Employment-Related Information, Sensory Information (audio/video recording), and any other categories of personal information you choose to share with us. We will use this information to evaluate your application for employment or an independent contractor role, as applicable. title: Intercompany Accountant
description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

We are looking for an Intercompany Accountant to support the Group's intercompany accounting processes across our international group, with a focus on cost-plus calculations, intercompany reconciliations, and period-end close.

This is a hands-on accounting role suited to someone who enjoys working with detailed financial data and resolving discrepancies. The role works closely with local finance teams and other Group Finance stakeholders across entities and time zones.

The role is responsible for the accurate, complete, and timely delivery of assigned intercompany accounting activities, from source-data validation and cost-plus calculations through posting, reconciliation, issue resolution, and close support. The position operates within approved accounting policies, intercompany agreements, methodologies, and control requirements, escalating material or unusual matters to the Intercompany Manager.

Work Location: Hybrid (Netherlands or United Kingdom) | Remote (other European countries)

Your responsibilities will include:

Cost-plus calculations and agreement support

  • Prepare end-to-end cost-plus calculations in accordance with approved intercompany agreements, methodologies, and mark-up rates.
  • Extract and validate cost data, identify eligible costs, and apply agreed allocation keys, exclusions, and mark-ups.
  • Maintain detailed calculation schedules, ensuring traceability to source accounting records and supporting documentation.
  • Calculate periodic intercompany charges and true-ups, and prepare the related journal entries for review and approval.
  • Coordinate with local finance teams to confirm cost inputs and ensure timely recording of charges by both counterparties.
  • Reconcile calculated charges to invoiced and recorded amounts, investigate differences, and prepare proposed corrections.
  • Support the maintenance of documentation required to evidence the application of approved intercompany agreements and cost-plus methodologies.

Reconciliations and discrepancy follow-up

  • Help with monthly intercompany profit-and-loss reconciliations and quarterly balance-sheet reconciliations using NetSuite reports and established templates.
  • Match transactions and balances between group entities by counterparty and currency.
  • Investigate differences arising from timing, foreign exchange, missing entries, incorrect coding, or other posting issues.
  • Follow up with local finance teams to obtain supporting information and track outstanding items through resolution.
  • Prepare proposed correcting entries for review and post approved adjustments.
  • Identify recurring mismatch patterns and communicate root causes and practical remediation actions to the Intercompany Manager.

Period-end close and reporting

  • Complete assigned intercompany close activities within agreed deadlines and in line with the Group close calendar.
  • Keep reconciliation trackers up to date, clearly documenting unresolved differences, follow-up actions, owners, and dependencies.
  • Provide clear explanations and supporting evidence for external audits, internal reviews, and other finance queries.
  • Communicate potential close risks early when required inputs, confirmations, or corrections are not received on time.

SOX and internal controls

  • Prepare and document a defined sub-set of the FSCP-REP control series related to intercompany processes

We expect you to have:

  • 5+ years of experience in accounting, preferably intercompany accounting or general ledger within an international or multi-entity organisation.
  • Practical experience preparing cost allocations, intercompany recharges, or cost-plus calculations is an advantage.
  • Strong Excel skills, including lookups and pivot tables.
  • Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP system; NetSuite experience is an advantage.
  • A degree or equivalent qualification in accounting, finance, or a related discipline.
  • Strong written and spoken English for communication with international finance teams.
  • Strong understanding of journal entries, account reconciliations, foreign currency (FX), and month-end close processes.
  • Ability to work confidently with large financial datasets, identify patterns in reconciliation differences, and document clear root-cause analysis.
  • Strong attention to detail and a structured approach to repetitive, deadline-driven accounting work.
  • Comfort working in a fast-changing, international and post-IPO environment where processes and responsibilities may evolve as the Group grows.
  • A collaborative approach and willingness to support colleagues across entities and time zones.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

The role in a nutshell


The Pupil Wellbeing Practitioner plays a key role in supporting pupils’ social, emotional and behavioural development, helping to create a safe, inclusive and positive learning environment where all children can thrive. Working with pupils who present with complex needs, the postholder will use therapeutic, restorative and positive behaviour support approaches to help pupils regulate emotions, develop resilience and successfully engage in learning.


The Pupil Wellbeing Practitioner will work collaboratively with teaching staff, wellbeing teams and wider professionals to remove barriers to learning, promote pupil wellbeing and contribute to improved educational outcomes. Through targeted interventions, individual support and proactive behaviour strategies, the role will have a direct impact on pupils’ personal development, wellbeing and achievement.

• Provide one-to-one support for individual pupils, helping them overcome barriers to learning and achieve their personalised outcomes.

• Develop, implement and review positive behaviour support strategies for individual pupils and groups.

• Use therapeutic and de-escalation approaches to support pupils in managing emotions and behaviours effectively.

• Build positive, trusting relationships with pupils, families and colleagues to promote engagement and wellbeing.

• Monitor, record and report on pupil progress, behaviour and wellbeing, contributing to planning and review processes.


Additional Responsibilities:

As part of this role, the Pupil Wellbeing Practitioner will also be a member of the Trust’s Team Teach Training Team. The postholder will support the planning and delivery of Team Teach training across the Trust, helping to ensure colleagues are equipped with effective strategies to build positive relationships, manage behaviour safely and promote a culture of inclusion and wellbeing.


This role offers variety and the opportunity to face something new each day. You may encounter different topics and challenges, but the rewards are significant. Supporting pupils to reach their potential, grow in confidence, and achieve their goals brings immense satisfaction.

title: Science Technician (Chemistry)
description:
Science Technician

Full Time

Permanent, Term Time only

The Henrietta Barnett School is a high-performing state grammar school with approximately 800 girls aged 11-18 and was awarded Top State School of the Year 2023 for Academic Achievement by The Sunday Times Parent Power Guide. It is known for its warm, friendly environment and ethos. This role is part of the Support Staff Team. The Science Department at HBS consists of eight laboratories, together with three preparation rooms and ancillary rooms located on one site, on split floors. There are currently ten Science teachers supported by three technicians.

Job Description

The key role of the Science Technician (Chemistry) is to provide the technician’s service to the Head of Chemistry and the other Heads of Science, as part of the team of Science Department technicians in the school and to contribute specialist knowledge, skills and services to all areas of the Science Curriculum and to the Chemistry Department in particular. The Science Technician team consists of a Senior Science Technician and two other technicians. The Science Technician (Chemistry) reports to the Senior Science Technician.

The following gives an overview of the responsibilities of the role. The list is not exhaustive and will adapt in consultation with the post-holder, as needs change and opportunities develop.

  • Preparing apparatus, materials and solutions, and setting up and checking equipment and apparatus for use in practical classes. Setting up and carrying out demonstrations. Retrieving and clearing away apparatus etc.

  • Arrange for the disposal of waste laboratory materials including chemical and biological waste in accordance with established and regulatory procedures and regulations. Disposal of equipment surplus to requirements.

  • Participate in the development of the Science Department practical and technical facilities to meet teaching and learning needs.

  • To be responsible for the maintenance and repair of departmental apparatus and equipment, and for maintenance records.

  • Under the direction of the Senior Technician, catalogue, prepare, issue and maintain materials, equipment, and stocktaking the same.

  • Maintaining stock levels and notifying the Senior Science Technician when stocks need to be replaced and ordered.

  • Assisting in checking stock books and keeping stock records

  • Check and store deliveries.

  • Ensure that all apparatus, equipment and chemicals are stored in accordance with regulations (CLEAPSS, COSHH).

  • To ensure the maintenance of laboratory services and facilities, liaising with the site manager as appropriate.

  • To ensure that the practical requirements of practical examinations/assessments are met, including preparing, setting up and testing materials, apparatus and equipment.

  • To give technical advice and assistance to teachers and other science technicians, assisting in practical classes as appropriate.

  • To advise teaching staff of technical requirements raised by the curriculum and to contribute to the department’s practical work, which includes work connected with Information Technology.

  • To ensure that satisfactory standards of safety and security are maintained at all times in accordance with the School’s policies and Health & Safety Regulations.

  • Other appropriate technician duties as reasonably requested by the Senior Technician, Heads of Department or other teachers in any areas of Science.

  • Playing a part in the Support Staff team across the school, including jobs such as assisting with Open Days and Entrance Examination Days.

  • Engaging in the school’s performance management programme.

  • Commitment to the Safeguarding and well-being of children and young people.

Person Specification

  • A Science-related degree would be desirable but is not essential.

  • Excellent communication skills, both written and oral.

  • Excellent spoken and written English

  • Efficient and effective organisational skills

  • Strong interpersonal skills and a good team player

  • Hard-working, punctual and committed

  • Honest, reliable, kind and a person of integrity

  • Ability to follow instructions

  • Calm under pressure

  • Ability to thrive in a busy school environment

  • Ability to be flexible and to ensure priorities are met, to work accurately under pressure, independently on your initiative and to prioritise effectively

  • Relevant experience within schools would be an advantage but not essential

Relevant training will be provided.

The Science Technician (Chemistry) reports to the Senior Science Technician.

Salary: SCP 4-10 Outer London £29,985 - £32,655 (FTE - 52 week calculation) depending on skills, qualifications and experience.

The role is advertised as full time (36 hours a week, 39 weeks) Term Time only. Application forms are available on the school website or from the Head’s PA, Mrs Claire Beetlestone on recruitment@hbschool.org.uk. Please email your completed form to Mrs Claire Beetlestone, including some lines explaining why you are suitable for the role. The closing date is 27th November 2026. Please note that applications may be considered in order they are received.

title: Inclusion Assistant
description:
Note: These are broad descriptions of the types of duties/activities expected at this level, for

illustrative purposes. They are not intended to provide an exhaustive list of duties.

POST TITLE: Inclusion Support Assistant

Overview:

We are seeking a highly organised, proactive and compassionate Inclusion Support Assistant to join our SEND and Inclusion Team. This varied role combines administrative, pastoral and pupil-facing responsibilities, including supporting SEND provision, coordinating records and communication, and delivering targeted interventions within the Inclusion Base. Working closely with pupils, families and staff, you will help remove barriers to learning and contribute to an inclusive environment where every young person can thrive. The successful candidate will have excellent organisational and communication skills, experience working with children or young people, and a passion for inclusive education.

Key Roles/Responsibilities

Administrative Support

  • Provide comprehensive administrative support to the SENDCo and Inclusion Team.
  • Coordinate meetings, Annual Reviews and appointments involving parents/carers, staff and external agencies.
  • Prepare, distribute and maintain meeting invitations, agendas, minutes and associated documentation.
  • Maintain accurate and confidential SEND records, ensuring pupil files and documentation are up to date and compliant with statutory requirements.
  • Support the completion, submission and administration of SEND documentation, referrals and related processes.
  • Assist in the preparation of reports and supporting evidence for review meetings, funding applications and statutory assessments.
  • Support the administration, monitoring and review of Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs).
  • Assist in the coordination and administration of access arrangements for assessments and examinations.
  • Support the planning and administration of SEND transition processes to ensure effective transfer of information and continuity of provision.
  • Monitor and support SEND attendance processes, liaising with relevant staff and families as appropriate.
  • Act as a first point of contact for routine SEND enquiries from parents, carers and external professionals.
  • Manage and triage SEND-related correspondence, ensuring enquiries are responded to promptly and directed to the appropriate member of staff.
  • Develop and maintain positive and professional relationships with families, promoting effective communication between home and school.
  • Provide information and signpost families to relevant internal and external support services where appropriate.
  • Support the organisation and delivery of parent consultation meetings, workshops and SEND-related events.
  • Manage and respond to low-level SEND concerns through professional dialogue, telephone communication and meetings with families.
  • Disseminate relevant SEND information, guidance and updates to staff to support inclusive practice across the school.
  • Deliver targeted one-to-one and small-group interventions under the direction of the SENDCo and Inclusion Team.
  • Provide effective support for pupils accessing the Inclusion Base, promoting engagement, wellbeing, independence and positive learning behaviours.
  • Monitor, track and evaluate the impact of intervention programmes, maintaining accurate records of attendance, progress and outcomes.
  • Provide timely feedback to the SENDCo and teaching staff regarding pupil engagement, progress and areas for further support.
  • Contribute to the planning and implementation of strategies that support the academic, social and emotional development of pupils with SEND.
  • Assist in the coordination and administration of Learning Support Assistant (LSA) timetables, deployment and associated records.
  • Support LSAs in maintaining accurate records, intervention documentation and administrative requirements.
  • Collate and organise evidence and information required for SEND reviews, monitoring activities and provision mapping.
  • Promote effective communication, collaboration and information sharing across the Inclusion Team.
  • Maintain the highest standards of confidentiality and data protection at all times.
  • Contribute to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people in accordance with school policies and statutory guidance.
  • Attend and participate in relevant meetings, training and professional development opportunities.
  • Support and uphold the school's vision, values and commitment to inclusive education.
  • Undertake any other duties commensurate with the grade and responsibilities of the post as reasonably requested by the SENDCo or Senior Leadership Team.

Communication and Family Liaison

Intervention and Inclusion Base Support

Support for Learning Support Assistants

General Responsibilities

Person Specification: Inclusion Support Assistant

Essential Qualifications

  • GCSE Grade 4/C or above (or equivalent) in English and Mathematics.
  • Commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people.

Essential Experience

  • Experience of working with children or young people in an educational, pastoral or support setting.
  • Experience of providing administrative support and maintaining accurate records.
  • Experience of building positive relationships with parents, carers and external professionals.
  • Experience of working as part of a team and contributing to shared goals.
  • Experience of supporting pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).

Desirable Experience

  • Experience of working within a school SEND or Inclusion Team.
  • Experience of delivering interventions, either on a one-to-one basis or in small groups.
  • Experience of supporting pupils with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs).
  • Experience of using school management information systems and SEND record-keeping systems.
  • Experience of coordinating meetings and communicating with external agencies.

Knowledge and Understanding

Essential

  • Understanding of SEND and inclusive educational practice.
  • Understanding of the barriers to learning experienced by pupils with additional needs.
  • Knowledge of safeguarding and child protection responsibilities.
  • Understanding of the importance of confidentiality and data protection.
  • Knowledge of effective strategies to support pupils' social, emotional and academic development.

Desirable

  • Knowledge of the SEND Code of Practice.
  • Understanding of the statutory processes relating to EHCPs and Annual Reviews.
  • Knowledge of access arrangements and examination support processes.

Skills and Abilities

Essential

  • Excellent organisational and administrative skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to establish positive and professional relationships with pupils, families, staff and external agencies.
  • Ability to manage and prioritise a varied workload effectively.
  • Ability to maintain accurate records and produce clear documentation.
  • Ability to work independently and use initiative when appropriate.
  • Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team.
  • Ability to support, motivate and engage pupils with a range of needs.
  • Competent IT skills, including the use of Microsoft Office applications.

Desirable

  • Ability to analyse and interpret data relating to pupil progress, attendance and interventions.
  • Ability to support the coordination of support staff and intervention programmes.

Personal Qualities

  • Genuine commitment to inclusion and ensuring the best outcomes for all pupils.
  • Compassionate, approachable and professional manner.
  • Resilient, adaptable and solution-focused.
  • High levels of integrity, discretion and professionalism.
  • Commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion.
  • Positive attitude and willingness to undertake professional development.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with sensitive situations.
  • Enthusiastic and committed to making a positive difference to the lives of children and young people.

Special Requirements

  • Satisfactory enhanced DBS clearance and all relevant pre-employment checks.
  • Commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people.
  • Willingness to attend relevant training and meetings as required.

Key Personal Attributes for Success in the Role

The successful candidate will be highly organised, empathetic and proactive, with a genuine passion for supporting children and young people with SEND. They will be equally comfortable managing administrative responsibilities, liaising with families and external agencies, and delivering targeted support and interventions to pupils within the Inclusion Base and across the school.

description:

We are seeking an exceptional SEND Improvement Lead to help drive our ambition for every pupil with SEND to thrive.

Inclusion is a key priority in our Corporate Strategy up to 2032, and we have a detailed Inclusion Strategy that we have started to implement with our 36 schools in line with the national agenda on Inclusion and the SEND Reforms.

title: Lead Teacher of Reading Intervention - Secondary
description:
We are a highly supportive school, backed by strong subject leadership and senior management, dedicated to fostering professional development and excellence in teaching and learning. We are seeking a highly ambitious, committed and dynamic professional to take on the newly created role of Lead Teacher of Reading Intervention. This is an exciting opportunity for an individual who is passionate about literacy and committed to improving outcomes for students who require intensive reading support.

The successful candidate will lead and deliver our reading intervention strategy for students Years 7 to 11 whose reading skills are significantly below age-related expectations. Working directly with some of our most vulnerable learners, you will help students develop the reading, phonics, and literacy skills they need to access the secondary curriculum successfully.

The postholder will be line managed by a member of the Senior Leadership Team and will work closely with the Secondary Literacy Lead, SEND and Inclusion Teams, curriculum leaders and families to ensure targeted support is effective and impactful. The role will also involve working cross-phase with primary colleagues where appropriate, supporting continuity in reading provision and successful transition into secondary education.

The role would particularly suit an experienced primary practitioner with a strong understanding of phonics, reading development and literacy intervention who is ready for the challenge of working in a secondary setting. Equally, we welcome applications from secondary colleagues with expertise in reading intervention. The successful candidate will be passionate about securing rapid progress for students whose low reading ages act as a barrier to learning.

The successful candidate will lead the assessment of reading and spelling ages across the Academy, co-ordinate diagnostic assessments, analyse literacy data and evaluate the impact of interventions. They will use this information to develop a coherent programme of support that is evidence-informed, targeted and responsible to student need.

Intervention delivery forms a central part of the role. The successful candidate will plan and deliver high-quality one-to-one, small-group, timetabled literacy interventions, adapting provision to meet individual needs and ensuring accelerated progress in reading. They will create an inclusive environment where students develop confidence and success as readers. The role may also include teaching some KS3 English, where appropriate, to further support students’ literacy development and access to the wider curriculum.

Collaboration is at the heart of this role. The successful candidate will work closely with curriculum leaders to identify barriers within different subject areas and support staff in developing strategies that improve literacy across the curriculum. They will also engage positively with parents and carers and contribute to the Academy’s wider literacy strategy.

The successful candidate will have a passion for teaching and learning, excellent communication and organisational skills, and a strong understanding of literacy development and intervention planning. Experience of phonics teaching and supporting young people with significant reading gaps will be essential. Above all, they will share our determination that every student, regardless of starting point, can access, engage with and succeed within the secondary curriculum through improved literacy and reading.

Visiting the school prior to submission of an application is warmly encouraged.

Our commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our children will be reflected throughout the recruitment process and the successful applicant will be subject to an enhanced DBS check and an online screening check.

Prospective candidates are encouraged to submit their applications as soon as possible as the school reserves the right to close the advert should we feel able to appoint an appropriate candidate.

title: Leisure Centre Duty Manager
description:
Are you passionate about the leisure industry and ready to take the next step in your career? Do you enjoy leading teams, delivering excellent customer service and ensuring leisure facilities operate safely and effectively?

We are looking for a motivated and enthusiastic Leisure Centre Duty Manager to join Lift Sir Herbert Leon Leisure Centre. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with previous leisure industry experience who is ready to take on a leadership role and contribute to the successful day-to-day management of a busy leisure facility.

About the role

As our Leisure Centre Duty Manager, you will play a key role in supporting the day-to-day operations of the Leisure Centre, ensuring a safe, welcoming and high-quality experience for all customers and visitors.

You will be responsible for supporting and supervising staff, maintaining high standards of customer service, ensuring compliance with health and safety regulations and contributing to the effective management of the Centre's facilities and activities.

Your responsibilities will include overseeing swimming pool operations, carrying out pool water tests and plant maintenance, lifeguarding swimming sessions and ensuring all facilities and equipment are maintained to a high standard.

You will also support staff recruitment, training and development, assist with the planning and delivery of leisure programmes and activities, and help promote the Centre's services to the wider community.

As part of the management team, you will act as a keyholder, support emergency procedures and ensure the Centre operates safely and efficiently in accordance with established policies and procedures.

About you

You will already hold an NPLQ Lifeguard Qualification and have previous experience working within a leisure centre environment. You will have strong team leadership skills and the confidence to support colleagues while maintaining excellent standards of service.

You will be:

  • Friendly, confident and customer-focused
  • An effective team leader who leads by example
  • Able to communicate effectively with colleagues and customers
  • Knowledgeable about leisure centre operations and committed to maintaining high standards of health and safety
  • Organised, reliable and able to respond effectively to operational challenges
  • Flexible and willing to support different areas of the Leisure Centre
  • Committed to providing a safe and welcoming environment for everyone using our facilities
  • Keen to contribute to the ongoing development and improvement of the Centre

GCSE Maths and English at Grade 4 or above, or an equivalent Level 2 qualification, are essential for the role.

Additional qualifications and experience, including a Level 1 or 2 Swimming Teacher Qualification, Pool Plant Operator Certificate, First Aid at Work Certificate or previous management experience, would be advantageous.

About Lift Sir Herbert Leon Leisure Centre

At the heart of our community, Lift Sir Herbert Leon Leisure Centre offers excellent fitness and sports facilities, including a swimming pool, gym, multi-purpose sports hall, 3G Astro-turf and grass pitches - everything needed to support active, healthy lifestyles for students and the local community.

As part of Lift Schools, you will be joining an organisation committed to ensuring every child receives an excellent education, in every classroom, every day.

Who is Lift Schools?

Lift Schools is made up of 62 primary, secondary and special schools, educating more than 35,000 pupils across the country. We believe education can transform lives - and we want every child in our schools to achieve their full potential.






This is a full-time position (37 hours per week), with a start date as soon as possible.

title: Finance Business Partner
description:
Finance Business Partner

Job Role: Finance Business Partner

Location: Newham Community Learning Trust Central Office, Pretoria Rd, London E16 4NP (Eastlea Community School)

Closing Date: 22nd November 2026

Newham Community Learning is a Multi-Academy Trust serving children and young people in East London. We believe every young person deserves an excellent education, whatever their background. Our commitment to equality and social justice shapes how we lead, how we spend, and how we hold ourselves to account.


About this Role

We are looking for an experienced and detail-focused finance Business Partner to join our Trust Finance Team. Working closely with the Chief Finance Officer and Financial Controller, you will play a key role in delivering accurate and effective financial accounting processes across the Trust, supporting strong financial controls, compliance and high-quality financial reporting.

You will take responsibility for a range of monthly and year-end accounting processes, including balance sheet and control account reconciliations, accruals and prepayments, intercompany transactions, trial balances, cashflow forecasting and fixed asset records. You will also prepare payroll journals and reconciliations, support VAT and statutory returns, and contribute to the annual external audit process, including ESFA and DfE reporting, HMRC and pension-related submissions.

Working closely with our schools, you will help ensure financial transactions are accurate, timely and compliant with Trust policies and procedures. You will also liaise with our payroll provider and work alongside the CFO, Financial Controller and Procurement Manager to ensure financial processes are robust, consistent and delivered within required deadlines.

The role will also provide an opportunity to contribute to the continued development and improvement of our financial accounting systems and processes, including PS Financials.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for someone who:

  • Has strong financial accounting experience and a sound understanding of accounting principles and financial controls.

  • Has experience of preparing and reviewing reconciliations, journals, accruals, prepayments and balance sheet accounts.

  • Is confident working with monthly and year-end financial processes and meeting strict deadlines.

  • Has excellent attention to detail and takes pride in ensuring financial information is accurate, complete and reliable.

  • Has experience supporting external audits, statutory accounts and financial returns.

  • Understands the importance of compliance, governance and financial procedures.

  • Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate discrepancies and resolve issues effectively.

  • Is confident working with financial systems and spreadsheets; experience of PS Financials would be advantageous.

  • Can communicate effectively with colleagues across schools, senior leaders, auditors and external organisations.

  • Is organised, proactive and able to manage competing priorities in a busy finance environment.

  • Works collaboratively and is committed to providing a high-quality financial service across the Trust

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional with strong financial accounting experience who is looking to make a meaningful contribution to a growing Trust and play an important role in maintaining high standards of financial management and accountability.

Why Join Us?

  • Be part of a forward-thinking multi-academy Trust, making a real impact on staff and students.

  • Local Government Pension Scheme.

  • Generous annual leave entitlement

  • A supportive, values-led culture in the heart of London.

  • Access to professional development and training opportunities.

  • Employee wellbeing initiatives and a focus on work-life balance.

location: Leeds, Yorkshire and the Humber, GB
description:
About the Role

Keighley College is looking for a Teacher of Hairdressing and Barbering to join our Hair and Beauty team.

You’ll teach across Levels 1 to 3, bringing your industry experience into the classroom and college salon to help students develop the skills, confidence, and professional standards they need for a career in the hair industry.

What You Will Do

  • You’ll deliver practical and theory sessions in hairdressing and barbering, from foundational cutting, styling and client consultation to more advanced colouring, clipper work, fading and beard shaping.
  • In our college salon, you’ll coach students as they work with clients, helping them develop their technical skills alongside safe working practices, client care and professional conduct.
  • You’ll adapt your teaching to suit students’ starting points, give clear feedback and track attendance and progress so you can intervene early when students need support.
  • You’ll prepare students for assessment and help them take their next steps into further study, apprenticeships or employment.
  • Working with colleagues and local employers, you’ll keep the curriculum up to date with industry practice and help students gain experience through employer-led projects and work placements.

About You

  • You’ll bring hands-on experience in hairdressing and barbering and be able to turn that experience into clear demonstrations and practical lessons for students from Level 1 to Level 3.
  • You’ll be as comfortable helping a beginner master their first cut as you are giving an advanced student precise feedback on a fade or colour service.
  • You’ll have up-to-date knowledge of salon and barbershop practice, including cutting, colouring, styling, clipper work and beard grooming.
  • You’ll model high standards of hygiene, safe working and client care, and help students understand what employers expect in a professional salon or barbershop.
  • You’ll communicate clearly, build positive relationships and adapt your approach to students’ different starting points.
  • You’ll give specific feedback that helps students improve their technique, build confidence and work more independently.
  • You’ll take an active role in supporting attendance, progress and achievement.
  • You’ll work well with colleagues and employers and be committed to safeguarding, inclusion and helping students progress into further study, apprenticeships or employment.

title: BA/Technical Product Manager
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://jobs.workable.com/company/u8TybTAE2YbYgRVFYov9t4/jobs-at-proarch

 Partner Discovery & Requirements Analysis
 • Lead and document working sessions with clinical, finance, operations, product, and technical stakeholders to understand existing workflows, business rules, data requirements, and operational processes.
• Translate manual and system-supported workflows into structured business and functional requirements.
• Produce gap-analysis documentation mapping current-state processes and partner requirements to existing platform capabilities.
• Classify requirements based on appropriate disposition, such as existing functionality, configuration, new development, acceptable operational workaround, shared platform enhancement, or out of scope.
• Maintain a consistent backlog structure across implementations so requirements remain comparable, traceable, and reusable.
 System Reconciliation & Technical Analysis
 • Analyze application logic, SQL, stored procedures, configuration parameters, integrations, and data flows to understand existing system behavior.
• Determine whether business requirements can be satisfied through configuration, existing functionality, process changes, or new development.
• Validate assumptions about platform behavior against available technical evidence and distinguish confirmed system behavior from inferred behavior.
• Identify discrepancies between documented behavior, stakeholder expectations, system configuration, and implemented logic.
• Trace business rules to underlying parameters, data elements, calculations, integrations, and system components.
• Identify where behaviors are configurable versus hardcoded and assess the impact on future implementations.
 Requirements Authoring
 • Write clear business and functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, assumptions, dependencies, open questions, and proposed workarounds.
• Maintain appropriate separation between business-facing requirements and technical implementation details.
• Ensure acceptance criteria reflect the agreed solution approach, including configuration changes, operational workarounds, or new functionality.
• Apply a consistent standard for distinguishing standalone requirements from assumptions, configuration decisions, implementation details, or operational procedures.
• Maintain traceability from business need through solution decision and development implementation.
 Cross-Functional Facilitation & Governance
 • Facilitate requirements, solutioning, and review sessions across business, clinical, product, engineering, data, and operational teams.
• Drive open questions toward resolution and update requirements and documentation to reflect confirmed decisions.
• Identify ambiguity, conflicting requirements, downstream impacts, and cross-feature dependencies before development begins.
• Prevent scope drift and ensure implementation-specific requirements do not unintentionally become platform-wide requirements.
• Support prioritization and decision-making by clearly communicating business impact, implementation complexity, dependencies, and risk.
 Ticket Creation & Scoping
 • Translate approved requirements into development-ready tickets containing problem statements, user stories, functional scope, acceptance criteria, dependencies, assumptions, and open questions.
• Partner with engineering and architecture teams to clarify technical scope and implementation approach.
• Track dependencies across features, integrations, implementations, and shared platform capabilities.
• Identify common capabilities that can support multiple clients, workflows, or future implementations rather than creating one-off solutions.

 • 8+ years of experience as a Business Analyst, Technical Product Manager, Product Owner, or equivalent role in a software-, data-, or technology-driven environment.
• Experience working within healthcare technology, healthcare operations, payer/provider systems, pharmacy, claims, revenue cycle, eligibility, or related healthcare domains.
• Ability to understand and reason about SQL, data structures, system logic, APIs, configuration, and technical workflows well enough to validate platform behavior and collaborate effectively with engineering teams.
• Demonstrated ability to write clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and development tickets that engineering teams can implement with minimal rework.
• Strong analytical rigor with the ability to distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions, challenge unclear reasoning, and validate conclusions.
• Experience facilitating requirements and solution-review sessions involving business, clinical, operational, and technical stakeholders.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt business and technical information for different audiences.
 Preferred Qualifications
 • Familiarity with healthcare claims, eligibility, reimbursement, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, or healthcare financial processes.
• Experience working with configurable or rules-driven healthcare platforms.
• Experience supporting client, provider, health system, or partner implementations.
• Understanding of data pipelines, ETL processes, APIs, healthcare integrations, and data exchange concepts.
• Experience managing a shared product backlog across multiple customers, implementations, or business units.
• Familiarity with healthcare data standards, regulatory requirements, or privacy considerations such as HIPAA.
 Key Competencies
 • Requirements elicitation and translation
• Healthcare workflow analysis
• Technical and data analysis
• System behavior reconciliation
• Product and backlog management
• Stakeholder facilitation and decision-driving
• Cross-functional collaboration
• Analytical rigor and structured problem-solving
• Dependency and impact analysis
• Documentation discipline and traceability

title: Senior Backend Cloud Engineer
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: http://www.halcyon.ai

 What we do:
Halcyon is the industry’s first dedicated, adaptive security platform that combines multiple proprietary advanced prevention engines along with AI models focused specifically on stopping ransomware.

 Who we are:
Halcyon was formed in 2021 by a team of cyber industry veterans after battling the scourge of ransomware (and advanced threats) for years at some of the largest global security vendors. Comprised of leaders from Cylance (now Blackberry), Accuvant (now Optiv), Fireye and ISS X-Force (now IBM), Halcyon is focused on building products and solutions for mid-market and enterprise customers.

 As a remote-native, completely distributed global team, we recognize great talent can exist anywhere. We invite you to apply to a job you’re interested in and we'll work a plan to meet your needs.

 The Role

 At Halcyon, we’re building a world-class anti-ransomware platform grounded in innovation and resilience. As part of that vision, we’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our cloud team. You’ll lead the development and evolution of our data platform and API services, working within a modern tech stack that blends Scala and Rust.

 You’ll join a team focused on building scalable, maintainable backend systems that serve both internal and customer-facing functions. Your primary focus will be on Rust and Scala services, with opportunities to shape our transition to Rust where it makes sense. Python development experience is highly valued, particularly for supporting our security analysis platform which includes malware analysis engines, automated threat detection, and machine learning workflows.

 Responsibilities

• Lead the design and delivery of features across our data platform and public API services, including ingestion, transformation, and enrichment of security data.

• Drive system design, architecture, and data flow decisions in partnership with product and platform engineering.

• Build, deploy, and own Scala-based backend services in production, keeping them reliable, secure, and performant.

• Help shape and execute our migration of selected APIs from Scala to Rust, ensuring consistency and continuity along the way.

• Set the bar for code quality, documentation, and operational excellence.

• Lead design reviews, code reviews and take part in on-call and incident response.

• Support and enhance our Python-based security analysis platform, including malware analysis engines, automated threat detection, and machine learning model workflows.

 Skills and Qualifications

• 5+ years of backend engineering experience, with recent experience in a JVM-based codebase.

• A track record of designing and owning distributed systems from start to finish.

• Experience with Rust, or a well-formed view of when it’s the right tool, and the ability to help guide a migration.

• Strong understanding of APIs, messaging systems (Kafka), and modern data stores (Postgres, DynamoDB, OpenSearch).

• Experience building services in a cloud-native environment, preferably AWS.

• Working knowledge of containers and Kubernetes.

• Comfortable working in a remote-first, asynchronous team environment.

 Bonus Skills and Qualifications

• Familiarity with functional programming patterns and idiomatic Scala.

• Experience with Databricks and ClickHouse (or similar lakehouse and analytical/OLAP data stores).

• Experience with Terraform, Helm, and GitHub Actions.

• Familiarity with observability tools (Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch).

• Prior work on security products, data pipelines, or high-availability systems.

• Python development experience, particularly with security analysis tools and malware detection frameworks (YARA, PE analysis, binary analysis).

• Familiarity with machine learning workflows, AutoML, and MLflow for model deployment and management.

• Experience with binary analysis libraries (LIEF, ssdeep, TLSH) and security tooling integration.

 Benefits:

 Halcyon offers the following benefits to eligible employees:

•
 Comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, and vision) with premiums paid in full for employees and dependents.

•
 401k plan with a generous employer contribution.

•
 Short and long-term disability coverage, basic life and AD&D insurance plans.

•
 Medical and dependent care FSA options.

•
 Flexible PTO policy.

•
 Parental leave.

•
 Generous equity offering.

 The Company reserves the right to modify or change these benefits programs at any time, with or without notice.​

 Base Salary Range : $120,000 - $170,000

 Bonus Target: 10%
 In accordance with applicable state and federal laws, the range provided is Halcyon’s reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and location. Base pay is one part of the total package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and equity in the Company.

 We understand it takes a diverse team of highly intelligent, passionate, curious, and creative people to develop the exceptional product we are building. Our dynamic team has incredible perspectives to share, just as we know you do, and we take great pride in being an equal opportunity employer.
